2398	   illustrate some use cases for SRTP, and give some guidelines for
2399	   recommended setting of its options.
2400	
2401	11.1.  Unicast
2402	
2403	   A typical example would be a voice call or video-on-demand
2404	   application.
2405	
2406	
2407	
2408	
2409	
2410	Baugher, et al.             Standards Track                    [Page 43]
2411	 
2412	RFC 3711                          SRTP                        March 2004
2413	
2414	
2415	   Consider one bi-directional RTP stream, as one RTP session.  It is
2416	   possible for the two parties to share the same master key in the two
2417	   directions according to the principles of Section 9.1.  The first
2418	   round of the key derivation splits the master key into any or all of
2419	   the following session keys (according to the provided security
2420	   functions):
2421	
2422	   SRTP_encr_key, SRTP_auth_key, SRTCP_encr_key, and SRTCP_auth key.
2423	
2424	   (For simplicity, we omit discussion of the salts, which are also
2425	   derived.)  In this scenario, it will in most cases suffice to have a
2426	   single master key with the default lifetime.  This guarantees
2427	   sufficiently long lifetime of the keys and a minimum set of keys in
2428	   place for most practical purposes.  Also, in this case RTCP
2429	   protection can be applied smoothly.  Under these assumptions, use of
2430	   the MKI can be omitted.  As the key-derivation in combination with
2431	   large difference in the packet rate in the respective directions may
2432	   require simultaneous storage of several session keys, if storage is
2433	   an issue, we recommended to use low-rate key derivation.
2434	
2435	   The same considerations can be extended to the unicast scenario with
2436	   multiple RTP sessions, where each session would have a distinct
2437	   master key.
2438	
2439	11.2.  Multicast (one sender)
2440	
2441	   Just as with (unprotected) RTP, a scalability issue arises in big
2442	   groups due to the possibly very large amount of SRTCP Receiver
2443	   Reports that the sender might need to process.  In SRTP, the sender
2444	   may have to keep state (the cryptographic context) for each receiver,
2445	   or more precisely, for the SRTCP used to protect Receiver Reports.
2446	   The overhead increases proportionally to the size of the group.  In
2447	   particular, re-keying requires special concern, see below.
2448	
2449	   Consider first a small group of receivers.  There are a few possible
2450	   setups with the distribution of master keys among the receivers.
2451	   Given a single RTP session, one possibility is that the receivers
2452	   share the same master key as per Section 9.1 to secure all their
2453	   respective RTCP traffic.  This shared master key could then be the
2454	   same one used by the sender to protect its outbound SRTP traffic.
2455	   Alternatively, it could be a master key shared only among the
2456	   receivers and used solely for their SRTCP traffic.  Both alternatives
2457	   require the receivers to trust each other.
2458	
2459	   Considering SRTCP and key storage, it is recommended to use low-rate
2460	   (or zero) key_derivation (except the mandatory initial one), so that
2461	   the sender does not need to store too many session keys (each SRTCP
2462	   stream might otherwise have a different session key at a given point
2463	
2464	
2465	
2466	Baugher, et al.             Standards Track                    [Page 44]
2467	 
2468	RFC 3711                          SRTP                        March 2004
2469	
2470	
2471	   in time, as the SRTCP sources send at different times).  Thus, in
2472	   case key derivation is wanted for SRTP, the cryptographic context for
2473	   SRTP can be kept separate from the SRTCP crypto context, so that it
2474	   is possible to have a key_derivation_rate of 0 for SRTCP and a non-
2475	   zero value for SRTP.
2476	
2477	   Use of the MKI for re-keying is RECOMMENDED for most applications
2478	   (see Section 8.1).
2479	
2480	   If there are more than one SRTP/SRTCP stream (within the same RTP
2481	   session) that share the master key, the upper limit of 2^48 SRTP
2482	   packets / 2^31 SRTCP packets means that, before one of the streams
2483	   reaches its maximum number of packets, re-keying MUST be triggered on
2484	   ALL streams sharing the master key.  (From strict security point of
2485	   view, only the stream reaching the maximum would need to be re-keyed,
2486	   but then the streams would no longer be sharing master key, which is
2487	   the intention.)  A local policy at the sender side should force
2488	   rekeying in a way that the maximum packet limit is not reached on any
2489	   of the streams.  Use of the MKI for re-keying is RECOMMENDED.
2490	
2491	   In large multicast with one sender, the same considerations as for
2492	   the small group multicast hold.  The biggest issue in this scenario
2493	   is the additional load placed at the sender side, due to the state
2494	   (cryptographic contexts) that has to be maintained for each receiver,
2495	   sending back RTCP Receiver Reports.  At minimum, a replay window
2496	   might need to be maintained for each RTCP source.
2497	
2498	11.3.  Re-keying and access control
2499	
2500	   Re-keying may occur due to access control (e.g., when a member is
2501	   removed during a multicast RTP session), or for pure cryptographic
2502	   reasons (e.g., the key is at the end of its lifetime).  When using
2503	   SRTP default transforms, the master key MUST be replaced before any
2504	   of the index spaces are exhausted for any of the streams protected by
2505	   one and the same master key.
2506	
2507	   How key management re-keys SRTP implementations is out of scope, but
2508	   it is clear that there are straightforward ways to manage keys for a
2509	   multicast group.  In one-sender multicast, for example, it is
2510	   typically the responsibility of the sender to determine when a new
2511	   key is needed.  The sender is the one entity that can keep track of
2512	   when the maximum number of packets has been sent, as receivers may
2513	   join and leave the session at any time, there may be packet loss and
2514	   delay etc.  In scenarios other than one-sender multicast, other
2515	   methods can be used.  Here, one must take into consideration that key
2516	   exchange can be a costly operation, taking several seconds for a
2517	   single exchange.  Hence, some time before the master key is
2518	   exhausted/expires, out-of-band key management is initiated, resulting
2519	
2520	
2521	
2522	Baugher, et al.             Standards Track                    [Page 45]
2523	 
2524	RFC 3711                          SRTP                        March 2004
2525	
2526	
2527	   in a new master key that is shared with the receiver(s).  In any
2528	   event, to maintain synchronization when switching to the new key,
2529	   group policy might choose between using the MKI and the <From, To>,
2530	   as described in Section 8.1.
2531	
2532	   For access control purposes, the <From, To> periods are set at the
2533	   desired granularity, dependent on the packet rate.  High rate re-
2534	   keying can be problematic for SRTCP in some large-group scenarios.
2535	   As mentioned, there are potential problems in using the SRTP index,
2536	   rather than the SRTCP index, for determining the master key.  In
2537	   particular, for short periods during switching of master keys, it may
2538	   be the case that SRTCP packets are not under the current master key
2539	   of the correspondent SRTP.  Therefore, using the MKI for re-keying in
2540	   such scenarios will produce better results.
2541	
2542	11.4.  Summary of basic scenarios
2543	
2544	   The description of these scenarios highlights some recommendations on
2545	   the use of SRTP, mainly related to re-keying and large scale
2546	   multicast:
2547	
2548	   - Do not use fast re-keying with the <From, To> feature.  It may, in
2549	     particular, give problems in retrieving the correct SRTCP key, if
2550	     an SRTCP packet arrives close to the re-keying time.  The MKI
2551	     SHOULD be used in this case.
2552	
2553	   - If multiple SRTP streams in the same RTP session share the same
2554	     master key, also moderate rate re-keying MAY have the same
2555	     problems, and the MKI SHOULD be used.
2556	
2557	   - Though offering increased security, a non-zero key_derivation_rate
2558	     is NOT RECOMMENDED when trying to minimize the number of keys in
2559	     use with multiple streams.
2560	
2561	12.  IANA Considerations
2562	
2563	   The RTP specification establishes a registry of profile names for use
2564	   by higher-level control protocols, such as the Session Description
2565	   Protocol (SDP), to refer to transport methods.  This profile
2566	   registers the name "RTP/SAVP".
2567	
2568	   SRTP uses cryptographic transforms which a key management protocol
2569	   signals.  It is the task of each particular key management protocol
2570	   to register the cryptographic transforms or suites of transforms with
2571	   IANA.  The key management protocol conveys these protocol numbers,
2572	   not SRTP, and each key management protocol chooses the numbering
2573	   scheme and syntax that it requires.
2574	
2575	
2576	
2577	
2578	Baugher, et al.             Standards Track                    [Page 46]
2579	 
2580	RFC 3711                          SRTP                        March 2004
2581	
2582	
2583	   Specification of a key management protocol for SRTP is out of scope
2584	   here.  Section 8.2, however, provides guidance on the parameters that
2585	   need to be defined for the default and mandatory transforms.

## 10. Interaction with Forward Error Correction mechanisms | 10. 与前向纠错机制的交互

#### 原文

The default processing when using Forward Error Correction (e.g., RFC 2733) processing with SRTP SHALL be to perform FEC processing prior to SRTP processing on the sender side and to perform SRTP processing prior to FEC processing on the receiver side. Any change to this ordering (reversing it, or, placing FEC between SRTP encryption and SRTP authentication) SHALL be signaled out of band.

#### 中文

在使用前向纠错（例如 RFC 2733）与 SRTP 结合处理时的默认处理方式为：在发送端，先执行 FEC 处理，再执行 SRTP 处理；在接收端，先执行 SRTP 处理，再执行 FEC 处理。对此顺序的任何更改（反转顺序，或将 FEC 置于 SRTP 加密与 SRTP 认证之间）都必须通过带外方式发出信号。

---

## 11. Scenarios | 11. 应用场景

#### 原文

SRTP can be used as security protocol for the RTP/RTCP traffic in many different scenarios. SRTP has a number of configuration options, in particular regarding key usage, and can have impact on the total performance of the application according to the way it is used. Hence, the use of SRTP is dependent on the kind of scenario and application it is used with. In the following, we briefly illustrate some use cases for SRTP, and give some guidelines for recommended setting of its options.

#### 中文

SRTP 可在许多不同的场景中用作 RTP/RTCP 流量的安全协议。SRTP 具有许多配置选项，特别是在密钥使用方面，并且根据使用方式的不同，可能会对应用的整体性能产生影响。因此，SRTP 的使用取决于其所应用的场景和应用类型。在下文中，我们简要说明 SRTP 的一些用例，并对其选项的推荐设置给出一些指导。

---

### 11.1. Unicast | 11.1. 单播

#### 原文

A typical example would be a voice call or video-on-demand application.

#### 中文

一个典型的例子是语音通话或视频点播应用。

---

#### 原文

Consider one bi-directional RTP stream, as one RTP session. It is possible for the two parties to share the same master key in the two directions according to the principles of Section 9.1. The first round of the key derivation splits the master key into any or all of the following session keys (according to the provided security functions):

SRTP_encr_key, SRTP_auth_key, SRTCP_encr_key, and SRTCP_auth key.

#### 中文

考虑一个双向 RTP 流，作为一个 RTP 会话。根据第 9.1 节的原则，双方可以在两个方向上共享相同的主密钥。第一轮密钥派生将主密钥分割为以下任意或全部会话密钥（根据所提供的安全功能）：

SRTP_encr_key、SRTP_auth_key、SRTCP_encr_key 和 SRTCP_auth key。

---

#### 原文

(For simplicity, we omit discussion of the salts, which are also derived.) In this scenario, it will in most cases suffice to have a single master key with the default lifetime. This guarantees sufficiently long lifetime of the keys and a minimum set of keys in place for most practical purposes. Also, in this case RTCP protection can be applied smoothly. Under these assumptions, use of the MKI can be omitted. As the key-derivation in combination with large difference in the packet rate in the respective directions may require simultaneous storage of several session keys, if storage is an issue, we recommended to use low-rate key derivation.

#### 中文

（为简化起见，我们省略了对同样会被派生出来的 salts 的讨论。）在此场景中，大多数情况下使用具有默认生命周期的单个主密钥就足够了。这保证了密钥具有足够长的生命周期，并且在大多数实际用途中只需要维护最少数量的密钥。此外，在这种情况下，RTCP 保护可以顺利应用。基于这些假设，可以省略 MKI 的使用。由于密钥派生加上两个方向上数据包速率的巨大差异可能需要同时存储多个会话密钥，如果存储空间是一个问题，我们建议使用低速率的密钥派生。

---

#### 原文

The same considerations can be extended to the unicast scenario with multiple RTP sessions, where each session would have a distinct master key.

#### 中文

同样的考虑可以扩展到具有多个 RTP 会话的单播场景，其中每个会话将拥有不同的主密钥。

---

### 11.2. Multicast (one sender) | 11.2. 多播（单个发送者）

#### 原文

Just as with (unprotected) RTP, a scalability issue arises in big groups due to the possibly very large amount of SRTCP Receiver Reports that the sender might need to process. In SRTP, the sender may have to keep state (the cryptographic context) for each receiver, or more precisely, for the SRTCP used to protect Receiver Reports. The overhead increases proportionally to the size of the group. In particular, re-keying requires special concern, see below.

#### 中文

与（未受保护的）RTP 一样，在大型分组中会出现可扩展性问题，因为发送者可能需要处理非常大量的 SRTCP 接收者报告（Receiver Reports）。在 SRTP 中，发送者可能需要为每个接收者维护状态（加密上下文），或者更确切地说，为用于保护接收者报告的 SRTCP 维护状态。开销会随着分组的大小成比例增加。特别是，密钥更新（re-keying）需要特别关注，见下文。

---

#### 原文

Consider first a small group of receivers. There are a few possible setups with the distribution of master keys among the receivers. Given a single RTP session, one possibility is that the receivers share the same master key as per Section 9.1 to secure all their respective RTCP traffic. This shared master key could then be the same one used by the sender to protect its outbound SRTP traffic. Alternatively, it could be a master key shared only among the receivers and used solely for their SRTCP traffic. Both alternatives require the receivers to trust each other.

#### 中文

首先考虑一个小型接收者分组。接收者之间主密钥的分发有几种可能的设置。给定一个单一的 RTP 会话，一种可能性是接收者根据第 9.1 节共享相同的主密钥来保护其各自的全部 RTCP 流量。这个共享的主密钥可以与发送者用于保护其出站 SRTP 流量的密钥相同。或者，它可以是一个仅在接收者之间共享并仅用于其 SRTCP 流量的主密钥。两种选择都需要接收者之间相互信任。

---

#### 原文

Considering SRTCP and key storage, it is recommended to use low-rate (or zero) key_derivation (except the mandatory initial one), so that the sender does not need to store too many session keys (each SRTCP stream might otherwise have a different session key at a given point in time, as the SRTCP sources send at different times). Thus, in case key derivation is wanted for SRTP, the cryptographic context for SRTP can be kept separate from the SRTCP crypto context, so that it is possible to have a key_derivation_rate of 0 for SRTCP and a non-zero value for SRTP.

#### 中文

考虑到 SRTCP 和密钥存储，建议使用低速率（或零速率）的 key_derivation（除了强制性的初始派生），这样发送者就无需存储过多的会话密钥（否则，由于 SRTCP 源在不同的时间发送，每个 SRTCP 流在给定的时间点可能会有不同的会话密钥）。因此，如果需要为 SRTP 进行密钥派生，可以将 SRTP 的加密上下文与 SRTCP 的加密上下文分开维护，使得 SRTCP 的 key_derivation_rate 为 0，而 SRTP 的值为非零成为可能。

---

#### 原文

Use of the MKI for re-keying is RECOMMENDED for most applications (see Section 8.1).

#### 中文

对于大多数应用，建议（RECOMMENDED）使用 MKI 进行密钥更新（参见第 8.1 节）。

---

#### 原文

If there are more than one SRTP/SRTCP stream (within the same RTP session) that share the master key, the upper limit of 2^48 SRTP packets / 2^31 SRTCP packets means that, before one of the streams reaches its maximum number of packets, re-keying MUST be triggered on ALL streams sharing the master key. (From strict security point of view, only the stream reaching the maximum would need to be re-keyed, but then the streams would no longer be sharing master key, which is the intention.) A local policy at the sender side should force rekeying in a way that the maximum packet limit is not reached on any of the streams. Use of the MKI for re-keying is RECOMMENDED.

#### 中文

如果在同一 RTP 会话中存在多个共享主密钥的 SRTP/SRTCP 流，则上限为 2^48 个 SRTP 数据包 / 2^31 个 SRTCP 数据包意味着，在任何一个流达到其最大数据包数之前，必须（MUST）在所有共享该主密钥的流上触发密钥更新。（从严格的安全角度来看，只有达到最大值的流才需要更新密钥，但这样一来这些流将不再共享主密钥，而这正是设计意图所在。）发送端应实施本地策略来强制执行密钥更新，以确保任何流都不会达到最大数据包限制。建议（RECOMMENDED）使用 MKI 进行密钥更新。

---

#### 原文

In large multicast with one sender, the same considerations as for the small group multicast hold. The biggest issue in this scenario is the additional load placed at the sender side, due to the state (cryptographic contexts) that has to be maintained for each receiver, sending back RTCP Receiver Reports. At minimum, a replay window might need to be maintained for each RTCP source.

#### 中文

在具有单个发送者的大型多播中，同样的考虑与小型分组多播一样适用。此场景中最大的问题是发送端的额外负载，这是由于必须为每个发回 RTCP 接收者报告的接收者维护状态（加密上下文）。至少，可能需要为每个 RTCP 源维护一个重放窗口。

---

### 11.3. Re-keying and access control | 11.3. 密钥更新与访问控制

#### 原文

Re-keying may occur due to access control (e.g., when a member is removed during a multicast RTP session), or for pure cryptographic reasons (e.g., the key is at the end of its lifetime). When using SRTP default transforms, the master key MUST be replaced before any of the index spaces are exhausted for any of the streams protected by one and the same master key.

#### 中文

密钥更新可能由于访问控制而发生（例如，在多播 RTP 会话中移除某个成员时），或者出于纯粹的加密原因（例如，密钥已达到其生命周期的终点）。在使用 SRTP 默认变换时，必须在受同一个主密钥保护的任何流的索引空间耗尽之前，替换该主密钥。

---

#### 原文

How key management re-keys SRTP implementations is out of scope, but it is clear that there are straightforward ways to manage keys for a multicast group. In one-sender multicast, for example, it is typically the responsibility of the sender to determine when a new key is needed. The sender is the one entity that can keep track of when the maximum number of packets has been sent, as receivers may join and leave the session at any time, there may be packet loss and delay etc. In scenarios other than one-sender multicast, other methods can be used. Here, one must take into consideration that key exchange can be a costly operation, taking several seconds for a single exchange. Hence, some time before the master key is exhausted/expires, out-of-band key management is initiated, resulting in a new master key that is shared with the receiver(s). In any event, to maintain synchronization when switching to the new key, group policy might choose between using the MKI and the <From, To>, as described in Section 8.1.

#### 中文

密钥管理如何为 SRTP 实现执行密钥更新不在本规范的范围内，但很明显，存在直接的方法来管理多播组的密钥。例如，在单发送者多播中，通常由发送者负责确定何时需要新密钥。发送者是唯一能够跟踪已发送数据包最大数量何时达到的实体，因为接收者可能随时加入和离开会话，可能存在数据包丢失和延迟等。在单发送者多播之外的场景中，可以使用其他方法。此处，必须考虑到密钥交换可能是一个代价高昂的操作，单次交换可能需要数秒钟的时间。因此，在主密钥耗尽/过期之前的某个时间，应启动带外密钥管理，产生一个与接收者共享的新主密钥。无论如何，为了在切换到新密钥时保持同步，组策略可以在使用 MKI 和 <From, To> 之间进行选择，如第 8.1 节所述。

---

#### 原文

For access control purposes, the <From, To> periods are set at the desired granularity, dependent on the packet rate. High rate re-keying can be problematic for SRTCP in some large-group scenarios. As mentioned, there are potential problems in using the SRTP index, rather than the SRTCP index, for determining the master key. In particular, for short periods during switching of master keys, it may be the case that SRTCP packets are not under the current master key of the correspondent SRTP. Therefore, using the MKI for re-keying in such scenarios will produce better results.

#### 中文

出于访问控制的目的，<From, To> 周期根据数据包速率按所需粒度设置。在某些大型分组场景中，高速率的密钥更新可能对 SRTCP 造成问题。如前所述，使用 SRTP 索引而非 SRTCP 索引来确定主密钥存在潜在问题。特别是，在主密钥切换期间的短暂时段内，可能会出现 SRTCP 数据包不受对应 SRTP 当前主密钥保护的情况。因此，在此类场景中使用 MKI 进行密钥更新将产生更好的结果。

---

### 11.4. Summary of basic scenarios | 11.4. 基本场景总结

#### 原文

The description of these scenarios highlights some recommendations on the use of SRTP, mainly related to re-keying and large scale multicast:

- Do not use fast re-keying with the <From, To> feature. It may, in particular, give problems in retrieving the correct SRTCP key, if an SRTCP packet arrives close to the re-keying time. The MKI SHOULD be used in this case.

- If multiple SRTP streams in the same RTP session share the same master key, also moderate rate re-keying MAY have the same problems, and the MKI SHOULD be used.

- Though offering increased security, a non-zero key_derivation_rate is NOT RECOMMENDED when trying to minimize the number of keys in use with multiple streams.

#### 中文

对这些场景的描述突出了关于 SRTP 使用的一些建议，主要涉及密钥更新和大规模多播：

- 不要使用带 <From, To> 功能的快速密钥更新。特别是，如果 SRTCP 数据包在接近密钥更新时间点到达时，可能会导致检索正确 SRTCP 密钥的问题。在这种情况下，应该（SHOULD）使用 MKI。

- 如果在同一 RTP 会话中的多个 SRTP 流共享相同的主密钥，即使是中等速率的密钥更新也可能会（MAY）出现同样的问题，此时应该（SHOULD）使用 MKI。

- 尽管非零的 key_derivation_rate 可以提供更高的安全性，但在尝试最小化多个流使用的密钥数量时，不推荐（NOT RECOMMENDED）使用它。

## 12. IANA Considerations | 12. IANA 考虑事项

#### 原文

The RTP specification establishes a registry of profile names for use by higher-level control protocols, such as the Session Description Protocol (SDP), to refer to transport methods. This profile registers the name "RTP/SAVP".

#### 中文

RTP 规范建立了一个配置文件名称注册表，供更高级别的控制协议（如会话描述协议 SDP）用来引用传输方法。本配置文件注册了名称 "RTP/SAVP"。

---

#### 原文

SRTP uses cryptographic transforms which a key management protocol signals. It is the task of each particular key management protocol to register the cryptographic transforms or suites of transforms with IANA. The key management protocol conveys these protocol numbers, not SRTP, and each key management protocol chooses the numbering scheme and syntax that it requires.

#### 中文

SRTP 使用由密钥管理协议发出信号的加密变换。向 IANA 注册加密变换或变换套件是每个特定密钥管理协议的任务。传递这些协议编号的是密钥管理协议，而非 SRTP，并且每个密钥管理协议选择其所需的编号方案和语法。

---

#### 原文

Specification of a key management protocol for SRTP is out of scope here. Section 8.2, however, provides guidance on the parameters that need to be defined for the default and mandatory transforms.

#### 中文

SRTP 的密钥管理协议的规范不在本文范围内。然而，第 8.2 节提供了关于需要为默认和强制性变换定义的参数的指导。

20	   This document defines the Opus interactive speech and audio codec.
21	   Opus is designed to handle a wide range of interactive audio

231	1.  Introduction
232	
233	   The Opus codec is a real-time interactive audio codec designed to
234	   meet the requirements described in [REQUIREMENTS].  It is composed of
235	   a layer based on Linear Prediction (LP) [LPC] and a layer based on
236	   the Modified Discrete Cosine Transform (MDCT) [MDCT].  The main idea
237	   behind using two layers is as follows: in speech, linear prediction
238	   techniques (such as Code-Excited Linear Prediction, or CELP) code low
239	   frequencies more efficiently than transform (e.g., MDCT) domain
240	   techniques, while the situation is reversed for music and higher
241	   speech frequencies.  Thus, a codec with both layers available can
242	   operate over a wider range than either one alone and can achieve
243	   better quality by combining them than by using either one
244	   individually.
245	
246	   The primary normative part of this specification is provided by the
247	   source code in Appendix A.  Only the decoder portion of this software
248	   is normative, though a significant amount of code is shared by both
249	   the encoder and decoder.  Section 6 provides a decoder conformance
250	   test.  The decoder contains a great deal of integer and fixed-point
251	   arithmetic that needs to be performed exactly, including all rounding
252	   considerations, so any useful specification requires domain-specific
253	   symbolic language to adequately define these operations.
254	   Additionally, any conflict between the symbolic representation and
255	   the included reference implementation must be resolved.  For the
256	   practical reasons of compatibility and testability, it would be
257	   advantageous to give the reference implementation priority in any
258	   disagreement.  The C language is also one of the most widely
259	   understood, human-readable symbolic representations for machine
260	   behavior.  For these reasons, this RFC uses the reference
261	   implementation as the sole symbolic representation of the codec.
262	
263	   While the symbolic representation is unambiguous and complete, it is
264	   not always the easiest way to understand the codec's operation.  For
265	   this reason, this document also describes significant parts of the
266	   codec in prose and takes the opportunity to explain the rationale
267	   behind many of the more surprising elements of the design.  These
268	   descriptions are intended to be accurate and informative, but the
269	   limitations of common English sometimes result in ambiguity, so it is
270	   expected that the reader will always read them alongside the symbolic
271	   representation.  Numerous references to the implementation are
272	   provided for this purpose.  The descriptions sometimes differ from
273	   the reference in ordering or through mathematical simplification
274	   wherever such deviation makes an explanation easier to understand.

400	
401	2.  Opus Codec Overview
402	
403	   The Opus codec scales from 6 kbit/s narrowband mono speech to
404	   510 kbit/s fullband stereo music, with algorithmic delays ranging
405	   from 5 ms to 65.2 ms.  At any given time, either the LP layer, the
406	   MDCT layer, or both, may be active.  It can seamlessly switch between
407	   all of its various operating modes, giving it a great deal of
408	   flexibility to adapt to varying content and network conditions
409	   without renegotiating the current session.  The codec allows input
410	   and output of various audio bandwidths, defined as follows:
411	
412	   +----------------------+-----------------+-------------------------+
413	   | Abbreviation         | Audio Bandwidth | Sample Rate (Effective) |
414	   +----------------------+-----------------+-------------------------+
415	   | NB (narrowband)      |           4 kHz |                   8 kHz |
416	   |                      |                 |                         |
417	   | MB (medium-band)     |           6 kHz |                  12 kHz |
418	   |                      |                 |                         |
419	   | WB (wideband)        |           8 kHz |                  16 kHz |
420	   |                      |                 |                         |
421	   | SWB (super-wideband) |          12 kHz |                  24 kHz |
422	   |                      |                 |                         |
423	   | FB (fullband)        |      20 kHz (*) |                  48 kHz |
424	   +----------------------+-----------------+-------------------------+
425	
426	                                  Table 1
427	
428	   (*) Although the sampling theorem allows a bandwidth as large as half
429	   the sampling rate, Opus never codes audio above 20 kHz, as that is
430	   the generally accepted upper limit of human hearing.
431	
432	   Opus defines super-wideband (SWB) with an effective sample rate of
433	   24 kHz, unlike some other audio coding standards that use 32 kHz.
434	   This was chosen for a number of reasons.  The band layout in the MDCT
435	   layer naturally allows skipping coefficients for frequencies over
436	   12 kHz, but does not allow cleanly dropping just those frequencies
437	   over 16 kHz.  A sample rate of 24 kHz also makes resampling in the
438	   MDCT layer easier, as 24 evenly divides 48, and when 24 kHz is
439	   sufficient, it can save computation in other processing, such as
440	   Acoustic Echo Cancellation (AEC).  Experimental changes to the band
441	   layout to allow a 16 kHz cutoff (32 kHz effective sample rate) showed
442	   potential quality degradations at other sample rates, and, at typical
443	   bitrates, the number of bits saved by using such a cutoff instead of
444	   coding in fullband (FB) mode is very small.  Therefore, if an
445	   application wishes to process a signal sampled at 32 kHz, it should
446	   just use FB.
447	
448	
449	
450	Valin, et al.                Standards Track                    [Page 8]
451	 
452	RFC 6716                 Interactive Audio Codec          September 2012
453	
454	
455	   The LP layer is based on the SILK codec [SILK].  It supports NB, MB,
456	   or WB audio and frame sizes from 10 ms to 60 ms, and requires an
457	   additional 5 ms look-ahead for noise shaping estimation.  A small
458	   additional delay (up to 1.5 ms) may be required for sampling rate
459	   conversion.  Like Vorbis [VORBIS-WEBSITE] and many other modern
460	   codecs, SILK is inherently designed for variable bitrate (VBR)
461	   coding, though the encoder can also produce constant bitrate (CBR)
462	   streams.  The version of SILK used in Opus is substantially modified
463	   from, and not compatible with, the stand-alone SILK codec previously
464	   deployed by Skype.  This document does not serve to define that
465	   format, but those interested in the original SILK codec should see
466	   [SILK] instead.
467	
468	   The MDCT layer is based on the Constrained-Energy Lapped Transform
469	   (CELT) codec [CELT].  It supports NB, WB, SWB, or FB audio and frame
470	   sizes from 2.5 ms to 20 ms, and requires an additional 2.5 ms look-
471	   ahead due to the overlapping MDCT windows.  The CELT codec is
472	   inherently designed for CBR coding, but unlike many CBR codecs, it is
473	   not limited to a set of predetermined rates.  It internally allocates
474	   bits to exactly fill any given target budget, and an encoder can
475	   produce a VBR stream by varying the target on a per-frame basis.  The
476	   MDCT layer is not used for speech when the audio bandwidth is WB or
477	   less, as it is not useful there.  On the other hand, non-speech
478	   signals are not always adequately coded using linear prediction.
479	   Therefore, the MDCT layer should be used for music signals.
480	
481	   A "Hybrid" mode allows the use of both layers simultaneously with a
482	   frame size of 10 or 20 ms and an SWB or FB audio bandwidth.  The LP
483	   layer codes the low frequencies by resampling the signal down to WB.
484	   The MDCT layer follows, coding the high frequency portion of the
485	   signal.  The cutoff between the two lies at 8 kHz, the maximum WB
486	   audio bandwidth.  In the MDCT layer, all bands below 8 kHz are
487	   discarded, so there is no coding redundancy between the two layers.
488	
489	   The sample rate (in contrast to the actual audio bandwidth) can be
490	   chosen independently on the encoder and decoder side, e.g., a
491	   fullband signal can be decoded as wideband, or vice versa.  This
492	   approach ensures a sender and receiver can always interoperate,
493	   regardless of the capabilities of their actual audio hardware.
494	   Internally, the LP layer always operates at a sample rate of twice
495	   the audio bandwidth, up to a maximum of 16 kHz, which it continues to
496	   use for SWB and FB.  The decoder simply resamples its output to
497	   support different sample rates.  The MDCT layer always operates
498	   internally at a sample rate of 48 kHz.  Since all the supported
499	   sample rates evenly divide this rate, and since the decoder may
500	   easily zero out the high frequency portion of the spectrum in the
501	   frequency domain, it can simply decimate the MDCT layer output to
502	   achieve the other supported sample rates very cheaply.
503	
504	
505	
506	Valin, et al.                Standards Track                    [Page 9]
507	 
508	RFC 6716                 Interactive Audio Codec          September 2012
509	
510	
511	   After conversion to the common, desired output sample rate, the
512	   decoder simply adds the output from the two layers together.  To
513	   compensate for the different look-ahead required by each layer, the
514	   CELT encoder input is delayed by an additional 2.7 ms.  This ensures
515	   that low frequencies and high frequencies arrive at the same time.
516	   This extra delay may be reduced by an encoder by using less look-
517	   ahead for noise shaping or using a simpler resampler in the LP layer,
518	   but this will reduce quality.  However, the base 2.5 ms look-ahead in
519	   the CELT layer cannot be reduced in the encoder because it is needed
520	   for the MDCT overlap, whose size is fixed by the decoder.
521	
522	   Both layers use the same entropy coder, avoiding any waste from
523	   "padding bits" between them.  The hybrid approach makes it easy to
524	   support both CBR and VBR coding.  Although the LP layer is VBR, the
525	   bit allocation of the MDCT layer can produce a final stream that is
526	   CBR by using all the bits left unused by the LP layer.
527	
528	2.1.  Control Parameters
529	
530	   The Opus codec includes a number of control parameters that can be
531	   changed dynamically during regular operation of the codec, without
532	   interrupting the audio stream from the encoder to the decoder.  These
533	   parameters only affect the encoder since any impact they have on the
534	   bitstream is signaled in-band such that a decoder can decode any Opus
535	   stream without any out-of-band signaling.  Any Opus implementation
536	   can add or modify these control parameters without affecting
537	   interoperability.  The most important encoder control parameters in
538	   the reference encoder are listed below.
539	
540	2.1.1.  Bitrate
541	
542	   Opus supports all bitrates from 6 kbit/s to 510 kbit/s.  All other
543	   parameters being equal, higher bitrate results in higher quality.
544	   For a frame size of 20 ms, these are the bitrate "sweet spots" for
545	   Opus in various configurations:
546	
547	   o  8-12 kbit/s for NB speech,
548	
549	   o  16-20 kbit/s for WB speech,
550	
551	   o  28-40 kbit/s for FB speech,
552	
553	   o  48-64 kbit/s for FB mono music, and
554	
555	   o  64-128 kbit/s for FB stereo music.
556	
557	
558	
559	
560	
561	
562	Valin, et al.                Standards Track                   [Page 10]
563	 
564	RFC 6716                 Interactive Audio Codec          September 2012
565	
566	
567	2.1.2.  Number of Channels (Mono/Stereo)
568	
569	   Opus can transmit either mono or stereo frames within a single
570	   stream.  When decoding a mono frame in a stereo decoder, the left and
571	   right channels are identical, and when decoding a stereo frame in a
572	   mono decoder, the mono output is the average of the left and right
573	   channels.  In some cases, it is desirable to encode a stereo input
574	   stream in mono (e.g., because the bitrate is too low to encode stereo
575	   with sufficient quality).  The number of channels encoded can be
576	   selected in real-time, but by default the reference encoder attempts
577	   to make the best decision possible given the current bitrate.
578	
579	2.1.3.  Audio Bandwidth
580	
581	   The audio bandwidths supported by Opus are listed in Table 1.  Just
582	   like for the number of channels, any decoder can decode audio that is
583	   encoded at any bandwidth.  For example, any Opus decoder operating at
584	   8 kHz can decode an FB Opus frame, and any Opus decoder operating at
585	   48 kHz can decode an NB frame.  Similarly, the reference encoder can
586	   take a 48 kHz input signal and encode it as NB.  The higher the audio
587	   bandwidth, the higher the required bitrate to achieve acceptable
588	   quality.  The audio bandwidth can be explicitly specified in real-
589	   time, but, by default, the reference encoder attempts to make the
590	   best bandwidth decision possible given the current bitrate.
591	
592	2.1.4.  Frame Duration
593	
594	   Opus can encode frames of 2.5, 5, 10, 20, 40, or 60 ms.  It can also
595	   combine multiple frames into packets of up to 120 ms.  For real-time
596	   applications, sending fewer packets per second reduces the bitrate,
597	   since it reduces the overhead from IP, UDP, and RTP headers.
598	   However, it increases latency and sensitivity to packet losses, as
599	   losing one packet constitutes a loss of a bigger chunk of audio.
600	   Increasing the frame duration also slightly improves coding
601	   efficiency, but the gain becomes small for frame sizes above 20 ms.
602	   For this reason, 20 ms frames are a good choice for most
603	   applications.
604	
605	2.1.5.  Complexity
606	
607	   There are various aspects of the Opus encoding process where trade-
608	   offs can be made between CPU complexity and quality/bitrate.  In the
609	   reference encoder, the complexity is selected using an integer from 0
610	   to 10, where 0 is the lowest complexity and 10 is the highest.
611	   Examples of computations for which such trade-offs may occur are:
612	
613	   o  The order of the pitch analysis whitening filter [WHITENING],
614	
615	
616	
617	
618	Valin, et al.                Standards Track                   [Page 11]
619	 
620	RFC 6716                 Interactive Audio Codec          September 2012
621	
622	
623	   o  The order of the short-term noise shaping filter,
624	
625	   o  The number of states in delayed decision quantization of the
626	      residual signal, and
627	
628	   o  The use of certain bitstream features such as variable time-
629	      frequency resolution and the pitch post-filter.
630	
631	2.1.6.  Packet Loss Resilience
632	
633	   Audio codecs often exploit inter-frame correlations to reduce the
634	   bitrate at a cost in error propagation: after losing one packet,
635	   several packets need to be received before the decoder is able to
636	   accurately reconstruct the speech signal.  The extent to which Opus
637	   exploits inter-frame dependencies can be adjusted on the fly to
638	   choose a trade-off between bitrate and amount of error propagation.
639	
640	2.1.7.  Forward Error Correction (FEC)
641	
642	   Another mechanism providing robustness against packet loss is the in-
643	   band Forward Error Correction (FEC).  Packets that are determined to
644	   contain perceptually important speech information, such as onsets or
645	   transients, are encoded again at a lower bitrate and this re-encoded
646	   information is added to a subsequent packet.
647	
648	2.1.8.  Constant/Variable Bitrate
649	
650	   Opus is more efficient when operating with variable bitrate (VBR),
651	   which is the default.  When low-latency transmission is required over
652	   a relatively slow connection, then constrained VBR can also be used.
653	   This uses VBR in a way that simulates a "bit reservoir" and is
654	   equivalent to what MP3 (MPEG 1, Layer 3) and AAC (Advanced Audio
655	   Coding) call CBR (i.e., not true CBR due to the bit reservoir).  In
656	   some (rare) applications, constant bitrate (CBR) is required.  There
657	   are two main reasons to operate in CBR mode:
658	
659	   o  When the transport only supports a fixed size for each compressed
660	      frame, or
661	
662	   o  When encryption is used for an audio stream that is either highly
663	      constrained (e.g., yes/no, recorded prompts) or highly sensitive
664	      [SRTP-VBR].
665	
666	   Bitrate may still be allowed to vary, even with sensitive data, as
667	   long as the variation is not driven by the input signal (for example,
668	   to match changing network conditions).  To achieve this, an
669	   application should still run Opus in CBR mode, but change the target
670	   rate before each packet.
671	
672	
673	
674	Valin, et al.                Standards Track                   [Page 12]
675	 
676	RFC 6716                 Interactive Audio Codec          September 2012
677	
678	
679	2.1.9.  Discontinuous Transmission (DTX)
680	
681	   Discontinuous Transmission (DTX) reduces the bitrate during silence
682	   or background noise.  When DTX is enabled, only one frame is encoded
683	   every 400 milliseconds.
684	
685	3.  Internal Framing
686	
687	   The Opus encoder produces "packets", which are each a contiguous set
688	   of bytes meant to be transmitted as a single unit.  The packets
689	   described here do not include such things as IP, UDP, or RTP headers,
690	   which are normally found in a transport-layer packet.  A single
691	   packet may contain multiple audio frames, so long as they share a
692	   common set of parameters, including the operating mode, audio
693	   bandwidth, frame size, and channel count (mono vs. stereo).  This
694	   section describes the possible combinations of these parameters and
695	   the internal framing used to pack multiple frames into a single
696	   packet.  This framing is not self-delimiting.  Instead, it assumes
697	   that a lower layer (such as UDP or RTP [RFC3550] or Ogg [RFC3533] or
698	   Matroska [MATROSKA-WEBSITE]) will communicate the length, in bytes,

## Abstract | 摘要

#### 原文
This document defines the Opus interactive speech and audio codec.
Opus is designed to handle a wide range of interactive audio
applications, including Voice over IP, videoconferencing, in-game
chat, and even live, distributed music performances.  It scales from
low bitrate narrowband speech at 6 kbit/s to very high quality stereo
music at 510 kbit/s.  Opus uses both Linear Prediction (LP) and the
Modified Discrete Cosine Transform (MDCT) to achieve good compression
of both speech and music.

## 1. Introduction | 1. 引言

#### 原文
The Opus codec is a real-time interactive audio codec designed to
meet the requirements described in [REQUIREMENTS].  It is composed of
a layer based on Linear Prediction (LP) [LPC] and a layer based on
the Modified Discrete Cosine Transform (MDCT) [MDCT].  The main idea
behind using two layers is as follows: in speech, linear prediction
techniques (such as Code-Excited Linear Prediction, or CELP) code low
frequencies more efficiently than transform (e.g., MDCT) domain
techniques, while the situation is reversed for music and higher
speech frequencies.  Thus, a codec with both layers available can
operate over a wider range than either one alone and can achieve
better quality by combining them than by using either one
individually.

#### 中文
Opus 编解码器是一种实时交互式音频编解码器，旨在满足 [REQUIREMENTS] 中描述的需求。它由一个基于线性预测（LP）[LPC] 的层和一个基于修正离散余弦变换（MDCT）[MDCT] 的层组成。使用两个层的主要思想如下：在语音方面，线性预测技术（如码激励线性预测，或称 CELP）对低频的编码效率高于变换域（如 MDCT）技术，而对于音乐和较高的语音频率，情况则相反。因此，同时具备两种层的编解码器可以在比单独使用任何一种层更广的范围内运行，并且通过将两者结合使用，可以获得比单独使用任何一种更好的质量。

---

#### 原文
The primary normative part of this specification is provided by the
source code in Appendix A.  Only the decoder portion of this software
is normative, though a significant amount of code is shared by both
the encoder and decoder.  Section 6 provides a decoder conformance
test.  The decoder contains a great deal of integer and fixed-point
arithmetic that needs to be performed exactly, including all rounding
considerations, so any useful specification requires domain-specific
symbolic language to adequately define these operations.
Additionally, any conflict between the symbolic representation and
the included reference implementation must be resolved.  For the
practical reasons of compatibility and testability, it would be
advantageous to give the reference implementation priority in any
disagreement.  The C language is also one of the most widely
understood, human-readable symbolic representations for machine
behavior.  For these reasons, this RFC uses the reference
implementation as the sole symbolic representation of the codec.

#### 中文
本规范的主要规范性部分由附录 A 中的源代码提供。只有该软件的解码器部分是规范性的，尽管编码器和解码器共享大量代码。第 6 节提供了解码器一致性测试。解码器包含大量需要精确执行的整数和定点运算，包括所有舍入考虑，因此任何有用的规范都需要领域特定的符号语言来充分定义这些操作。此外，符号表示与所包含的参考实现之间的任何冲突都必须得到解决。出于兼容性和可测试性的实际原因，在任何分歧中给予参考实现优先地位将是有利的。C 语言也是最广泛理解、人类可读的机器行为符号表示之一。基于这些原因，本 RFC 将参考实现作为编解码器的唯一符号表示。

---

#### 原文
While the symbolic representation is unambiguous and complete, it is
not always the easiest way to understand the codec's operation.  For
this reason, this document also describes significant parts of the
codec in prose and takes the opportunity to explain the rationale
behind many of the more surprising elements of the design.  These
descriptions are intended to be accurate and informative, but the
limitations of common English sometimes result in ambiguity, so it is
expected that the reader will always read them alongside the symbolic
representation.  Numerous references to the implementation are
provided for this purpose.  The descriptions sometimes differ from
the reference in ordering or through mathematical simplification
wherever such deviation makes an explanation easier to understand.
For example, the right shift and left shift operations in the
reference implementation are often described using division and
multiplication in the text.  In general, the text is focused on the
"what" and "why" while the symbolic representation most clearly
provides the "how".

#### 中文
虽然符号表示是明确和完整的，但它并不总是理解编解码器操作的最简单方式。因此，本文档也用散文描述了编解码器的重要部分，并借此机会解释了设计中许多更令人惊讶的元素背后的原理。这些描述旨在准确和提供信息，但普通英语的局限性有时会导致歧义，因此希望读者始终将其与符号表示一起阅读。为此目的提供了许多对实现的引用。这些描述有时会在顺序上或通过数学简化而与参考实现有所不同，只要这种偏离使解释更容易理解。例如，参考实现中的右移和左移操作在文本中通常使用除法和乘法来描述。总的来说，文本侧重于"是什么"和"为什么"，而符号表示最清楚地提供了"怎么做"。

---

### 1.1. Notation and Conventions | 1.1. 符号与约定

#### 原文
The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT",
"SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this
document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119 [RFC2119].

#### 中文
本文档中的关键词 "MUST"、"MUST NOT"、"REQUIRED"、"SHALL"、"SHALL NOT"、"SHOULD"、"SHOULD NOT"、"RECOMMENDED"、"MAY" 和 "OPTIONAL" 应按照 RFC 2119 [RFC2119] 中的描述进行解释。

---

#### 原文
Various operations in the codec require bit-exact fixed-point
behavior, even when writing a floating point implementation.  The
notation "Q<n>", where n is an integer, denotes the number of binary
digits to the right of the decimal point in a fixed-point number.
For example, a signed Q14 value in a 16-bit word can represent values
from -2.0 to 1.99993896484375, inclusive.  This notation is for
informational purposes only.  Arithmetic, when described, always
operates on the underlying integer.  For example, the text will
explicitly indicate any shifts required after a multiplication.

#### 中文
编解码器中的各种操作需要比特精确的定点行为，即使在编写浮点实现时也是如此。符号"Q<n>"（其中 n 是一个整数）表示定点数中小数点右侧的二进制位数。例如，16 位字中的有符号 Q14 值可以表示从 -2.0 到 1.99993896484375（含）的值。此符号仅用于提供信息的目的。算术运算在被描述时，始终在底层整数上进行。例如，文本将明确指出乘法后所需的任何移位。

---

#### 原文
Expressions, where included in the text, follow C operator rules and
precedence, with the exception that the syntax "x**y" indicates x
raised to the power y.  The text also makes use of the following
functions.

#### 中文
文本中包含的表达式遵循 C 运算符规则和优先级，但语法 "x**y" 表示 x 的 y 次方。本文还使用了以下函数。

---

### 1.1.1. min(x,y) | 1.1.1. 最小值函数

#### 原文
The smallest of two values x and y.

#### 中文
两个值 x 和 y 中的较小者。

---

### 1.1.2. max(x,y) | 1.1.2. 最大值函数

#### 原文
The largest of two values x and y.

#### 中文
两个值 x 和 y 中的较大者。

---

### 1.1.3. clamp(lo,x,hi) | 1.1.3. 钳制函数

#### 原文
                     clamp(lo,x,hi) = max(lo,min(x,hi))

With this definition, if lo > hi, then lo is returned.

#### 中文
                     clamp(lo,x,hi) = max(lo,min(x,hi))

根据此定义，如果 lo > hi，则返回 lo。

---

### 1.1.4. sign(x) | 1.1.4. 符号函数

#### 原文
The sign of x, i.e.,

                                    ( -1,  x < 0
                          sign(x) = <  0,  x == 0
                                    (  1,  x > 0

#### 中文
x 的符号，即：

                                    ( -1,  x < 0
                          sign(x) = <  0,  x == 0
                                    (  1,  x > 0

---

### 1.1.5. abs(x) | 1.1.5. 绝对值函数

#### 原文
The absolute value of x, i.e.,

                             abs(x) = sign(x)*x

#### 中文
x 的绝对值，即：

                             abs(x) = sign(x)*x

---

### 1.1.6. floor(f) | 1.1.6. 下取整函数

#### 原文
The largest integer z such that z <= f.

#### 中文
满足 z <= f 的最大整数 z。

---

### 1.1.7. ceil(f) | 1.1.7. 上取整函数

#### 原文
The smallest integer z such that z >= f.

#### 中文
满足 z >= f 的最小整数 z。

---

### 1.1.8. round(f) | 1.1.8. 舍入函数

#### 原文
The integer z nearest to f, with ties rounded towards negative
infinity, i.e.,

                           round(f) = ceil(f - 0.5)

#### 中文
最接近 f 的整数 z，平局时向负无穷方向舍入，即：

                           round(f) = ceil(f - 0.5)

---

### 1.1.9. log2(f) | 1.1.9. 以 2 为底的对数函数

#### 原文
The base-two logarithm of f.

#### 中文
f 的以 2 为底的对数。

---

### 1.1.10. ilog(n) | 1.1.10. 整数二进制位数函数

#### 原文
The minimum number of bits required to store a positive integer n in
binary, or 0 for a non-positive integer n.

                              ( 0,                 n <= 0
                    ilog(n) = <
                              ( floor(log2(n))+1,  n > 0

Examples:

o  ilog(-1) = 0

o  ilog(0) = 0

o  ilog(1) = 1

o  ilog(2) = 2

o  ilog(3) = 2

o  ilog(4) = 3

o  ilog(7) = 3

#### 中文
以二进制存储正整数 n 所需的最小位数，对于非正整数 n 为 0。

                              ( 0,                 n <= 0
                    ilog(n) = <
                              ( floor(log2(n))+1,  n > 0

示例：

o  ilog(-1) = 0

o  ilog(0) = 0

o  ilog(1) = 1

o  ilog(2) = 2

o  ilog(3) = 2

o  ilog(4) = 3

o  ilog(7) = 3

---

## 2. Opus Codec Overview | 2. Opus 编解码器概述

#### 原文
The Opus codec scales from 6 kbit/s narrowband mono speech to
510 kbit/s fullband stereo music, with algorithmic delays ranging
from 5 ms to 65.2 ms.  At any given time, either the LP layer, the
MDCT layer, or both, may be active.  It can seamlessly switch between
all of its various operating modes, giving it a great deal of
flexibility to adapt to varying content and network conditions
without renegotiating the current session.  The codec allows input
and output of various audio bandwidths, defined as follows:

   +----------------------+-----------------+-------------------------+
   | Abbreviation         | Audio Bandwidth | Sample Rate (Effective) |
   +----------------------+-----------------+-------------------------+
   | NB (narrowband)      |           4 kHz |                   8 kHz |
   |                      |                 |                         |
   | MB (medium-band)     |           6 kHz |                  12 kHz |
   |                      |                 |                         |
   | WB (wideband)        |           8 kHz |                  16 kHz |
   |                      |                 |                         |
   | SWB (super-wideband) |          12 kHz |                  24 kHz |
   |                      |                 |                         |
   | FB (fullband)        |      20 kHz (*) |                  48 kHz |
   +----------------------+-----------------+-------------------------+

                                  Table 1

(*) Although the sampling theorem allows a bandwidth as large as half
the sampling rate, Opus never codes audio above 20 kHz, as that is
the generally accepted upper limit of human hearing.

#### 中文
Opus 编解码器覆盖从 6 kbit/s 窄带单声道语音到 510 kbit/s 全频带立体声音乐，算法延迟范围从 5 ms 到 65.2 ms。在任何给定时刻，LP 层、MDCT 层或两者都可能处于活动状态。它可以在各种运行模式之间无缝切换，从而具有极大的灵活性来适应变化的内容和网络条件，而无需重新协商当前会话。该编解码器允许各种音频带宽的输入和输出，定义如下：

   +----------------------+-----------------+-------------------------+
   | 缩写                 | 音频带宽        | 采样率（有效）          |
   +----------------------+-----------------+-------------------------+
   | NB (窄带/narrowband)       |           4 kHz |                   8 kHz |
   |                      |                 |                         |
   | MB (中带/medium-band)      |           6 kHz |                  12 kHz |
   |                      |                 |                         |
   | WB (宽带/wideband)         |           8 kHz |                  16 kHz |
   |                      |                 |                         |
   | SWB (超宽带/super-wideband) |          12 kHz |                  24 kHz |
   |                      |                 |                         |
   | FB (全频带/fullband)        |      20 kHz (*) |                  48 kHz |
   +----------------------+-----------------+-------------------------+

                                  表 1

(*) 虽然采样定理允许带宽高达采样率的一半，但 Opus 从不编码 20 kHz 以上的音频，因为这是公认的人类听觉上限。

---

#### 原文
Opus defines super-wideband (SWB) with an effective sample rate of
24 kHz, unlike some other audio coding standards that use 32 kHz.
This was chosen for a number of reasons.  The band layout in the MDCT
layer naturally allows skipping coefficients for frequencies over
12 kHz, but does not allow cleanly dropping just those frequencies
over 16 kHz.  A sample rate of 24 kHz also makes resampling in the
MDCT layer easier, as 24 evenly divides 48, and when 24 kHz is
sufficient, it can save computation in other processing, such as
Acoustic Echo Cancellation (AEC).  Experimental changes to the band
layout to allow a 16 kHz cutoff (32 kHz effective sample rate) showed
potential quality degradations at other sample rates, and, at typical
bitrates, the number of bits saved by using such a cutoff instead of
coding in fullband (FB) mode is very small.  Therefore, if an
application wishes to process a signal sampled at 32 kHz, it should
just use FB.

#### 中文
Opus 将超宽带（SWB）定义为有效采样率 24 kHz，这与某些其他使用 32 kHz 的音频编码标准不同。这样做是基于许多原因。MDCT 层中的频带布局自然允许跳过 12 kHz 以上的频率系数，但不允许仅干净地丢弃 16 kHz 以上的那些频率。24 kHz 的采样率也使得 MDCT 层的重采样更容易，因为 24 能整除 48，而且当 24 kHz 足够时，它可以节省其他处理中的计算量，例如声学回声消除（AEC）。实验性修改频带布局以允许 16 kHz 截止（32 kHz 有效采样率）的结果表明，在其他采样率下可能出现质量下降，并且在典型比特率下，使用这种截止而非全频带（FB）模式编码所节省的比特数非常少。因此，如果应用希望处理以 32 kHz 采样的信号，它应该直接使用 FB。

---

#### 原文
The LP layer is based on the SILK codec [SILK].  It supports NB, MB,
or WB audio and frame sizes from 10 ms to 60 ms, and requires an
additional 5 ms look-ahead for noise shaping estimation.  A small
additional delay (up to 1.5 ms) may be required for sampling rate
conversion.  Like Vorbis [VORBIS-WEBSITE] and many other modern
codecs, SILK is inherently designed for variable bitrate (VBR)
coding, though the encoder can also produce constant bitrate (CBR)
streams.  The version of SILK used in Opus is substantially modified
from, and not compatible with, the stand-alone SILK codec previously
deployed by Skype.  This document does not serve to define that
format, but those interested in the original SILK codec should see
[SILK] instead.

#### 中文
LP 层基于 SILK 编解码器 [SILK]。它支持 NB、MB 或 WB 音频以及从 10 ms 到 60 ms 的帧大小，并且需要额外的 5 ms 前瞻用于噪声整形估计。采样率转换可能需要少量额外延迟（最多 1.5 ms）。与 Vorbis [VORBIS-WEBSITE] 和许多其他现代编解码器一样，SILK 本身是为可变比特率（VBR）编码而设计的，不过编码器也可以产生恒定比特率（CBR）流。Opus 中使用的 SILK 版本与 Skype 先前部署的独立 SILK 编解码器有很大修改且不兼容。本文档不旨在定义该格式，对原始 SILK 编解码器感兴趣的读者应转而参阅 [SILK]。

---

#### 原文
The MDCT layer is based on the Constrained-Energy Lapped Transform
(CELT) codec [CELT].  It supports NB, WB, SWB, or FB audio and frame
sizes from 2.5 ms to 20 ms, and requires an additional 2.5 ms look-
ahead due to the overlapping MDCT windows.  The CELT codec is
inherently designed for CBR coding, but unlike many CBR codecs, it is
not limited to a set of predetermined rates.  It internally allocates
bits to exactly fill any given target budget, and an encoder can
produce a VBR stream by varying the target on a per-frame basis.  The
MDCT layer is not used for speech when the audio bandwidth is WB or
less, as it is not useful there.  On the other hand, non-speech
signals are not always adequately coded using linear prediction.
Therefore, the MDCT layer should be used for music signals.

#### 中文
MDCT 层基于约束能量重叠变换（CELT）编解码器 [CELT]。它支持 NB、WB、SWB 或 FB 音频以及从 2.5 ms 到 20 ms 的帧大小，并且由于重叠的 MDCT 窗口需要额外的 2.5 ms 前瞻。CELT 编解码器本身是为 CBR 编码而设计的，但与许多 CBR 编解码器不同，它不限于一组预定的速率。它在内部分配比特以精确填满任何给定的目标预算，而编码器可以通过逐帧改变目标来产生 VBR 流。当音频带宽为 WB 或更低时，MDCT 层不用于语音，因为它在这些场景中无用。另一方面，非语音信号并不总是能通过线性预测被充分编码。因此，MDCT 层应用于音乐信号。

---

#### 原文
A "Hybrid" mode allows the use of both layers simultaneously with a
frame size of 10 or 20 ms and an SWB or FB audio bandwidth.  The LP
layer codes the low frequencies by resampling the signal down to WB.
The MDCT layer follows, coding the high frequency portion of the
signal.  The cutoff between the two lies at 8 kHz, the maximum WB
audio bandwidth.  In the MDCT layer, all bands below 8 kHz are
discarded, so there is no coding redundancy between the two layers.

#### 中文
"混合（Hybrid）"模式允许以 10 或 20 ms 帧大小和 SWB 或 FB 音频带宽同时使用两个层。LP 层通过将信号重采样到 WB 来编码低频部分。MDCT 层随后编码信号的高频部分。两者之间的分界位于 8 kHz，即最大 WB 音频带宽处。在 MDCT 层中，所有低于 8 kHz 的频带都被丢弃，因此两个层之间没有编码冗余。

---

#### 原文
The sample rate (in contrast to the actual audio bandwidth) can be
chosen independently on the encoder and decoder side, e.g., a
fullband signal can be decoded as wideband, or vice versa.  This
approach ensures a sender and receiver can always interoperate,
regardless of the capabilities of their actual audio hardware.
Internally, the LP layer always operates at a sample rate of twice
the audio bandwidth, up to a maximum of 16 kHz, which it continues to
use for SWB and FB.  The decoder simply resamples its output to
support different sample rates.  The MDCT layer always operates
internally at a sample rate of 48 kHz.  Since all the supported
sample rates evenly divide this rate, and since the decoder may
easily zero out the high frequency portion of the spectrum in the
frequency domain, it can simply decimate the MDCT layer output to
achieve the other supported sample rates very cheaply.

#### 中文
采样率（与实际音频带宽相对）可以在编码器端和解码器端独立选择，例如，一个全频带信号可以被解码为宽带，反之亦然。这种方法确保发送方和接收方始终能够互操作，而无论其实际音频硬件的能力如何。在内部，LP 层始终以两倍于音频带宽的采样率运行，最高可达 16 kHz，并对 SWB 和 FB 继续使用该采样率。解码器只需对其输出进行重采样以支持不同的采样率。MDCT 层在内部始终以 48 kHz 的采样率运行。由于所有支持的采样率都能整除此采样率，并且解码器可以方便地在频域中将频谱的高频部分清零，因此它可以简单地抽取 MDCT 层输出来以极低的代价实现其他支持的采样率。

---

#### 原文
After conversion to the common, desired output sample rate, the
decoder simply adds the output from the two layers together.  To
compensate for the different look-ahead required by each layer, the
CELT encoder input is delayed by an additional 2.7 ms.  This ensures
that low frequencies and high frequencies arrive at the same time.
This extra delay may be reduced by an encoder by using less look-
ahead for noise shaping or using a simpler resampler in the LP layer,
but this will reduce quality.  However, the base 2.5 ms look-ahead in
the CELT layer cannot be reduced in the encoder because it is needed
for the MDCT overlap, whose size is fixed by the decoder.

#### 中文
在转换到共同的期望输出采样率之后，解码器简单地将两个层的输出相加。为了补偿每个层所需的不同前瞻量，CELT 编码器输入被延迟了额外的 2.7 ms。这确保了低频和高频同时到达。编码器可以通过对噪声整形使用较少的前瞻或在 LP 层中使用更简单的重采样器来减少这种额外延迟，但这会降低质量。然而，CELT 层中基础的 2.5 ms 前瞻不能在编码器中减少，因为它是 MDCT 重叠所必需的，其大小由解码器固定。

---

#### 原文
Both layers use the same entropy coder, avoiding any waste from
"padding bits" between them.  The hybrid approach makes it easy to
support both CBR and VBR coding.  Although the LP layer is VBR, the
bit allocation of the MDCT layer can produce a final stream that is
CBR by using all the bits left unused by the LP layer.

#### 中文
两个层使用相同的熵编码器，避免了它们之间任何来自"填充比特"的浪费。混合方法使得同时支持 CBR 和 VBR 编码变得容易。虽然 LP 层是 VBR，但 MDCT 层的比特分配可以通过使用 LP 层未使用的全部比特来产生一个 CBR 的最终流。

---

### 2.1. Control Parameters | 2.1. 控制参数

#### 原文
The Opus codec includes a number of control parameters that can be
changed dynamically during regular operation of the codec, without
interrupting the audio stream from the encoder to the decoder.  These
parameters only affect the encoder since any impact they have on the
bitstream is signaled in-band such that a decoder can decode any Opus
stream without any out-of-band signaling.  Any Opus implementation
can add or modify these control parameters without affecting
interoperability.  The most important encoder control parameters in
the reference encoder are listed below.

#### 中文
Opus 编解码器包含许多控制参数，这些参数可以在编解码器的正常运行期间动态更改，而无需中断从编码器到解码器的音频流。这些参数仅影响编码器，因为它们对比特流产生的任何影响都是带内信令的，因此解码器可以在没有任何带外信令的情况下解码任何 Opus 流。任何 Opus 实现都可以添加或修改这些控制参数而不影响互操作性。参考编码器中最重要的编码器控制参数列在下面。

---

### 2.1.1. Bitrate | 2.1.1. 比特率

#### 原文
Opus supports all bitrates from 6 kbit/s to 510 kbit/s.  All other
parameters being equal, higher bitrate results in higher quality.
For a frame size of 20 ms, these are the bitrate "sweet spots" for
Opus in various configurations:

o  8-12 kbit/s for NB speech,

o  16-20 kbit/s for WB speech,

o  28-40 kbit/s for FB speech,

o  48-64 kbit/s for FB mono music, and

o  64-128 kbit/s for FB stereo music.

#### 中文
Opus 支持从 6 kbit/s 到 510 kbit/s 的所有比特率。在所有其他参数相同的情况下，更高的比特率带来更高的质量。对于 20 ms 的帧大小，以下是 Opus 在各种配置下的比特率"甜点（sweet spots）"：

o  对于 NB 语音：8-12 kbit/s，

o  对于 WB 语音：16-20 kbit/s，

o  对于 FB 语音：28-40 kbit/s，

o  对于 FB 单声道音乐：48-64 kbit/s，

o  对于 FB 立体声音乐：64-128 kbit/s。

---

### 2.1.2. Number of Channels (Mono/Stereo) | 2.1.2. 通道数（单声道/立体声）

#### 原文
Opus can transmit either mono or stereo frames within a single
stream.  When decoding a mono frame in a stereo decoder, the left and
right channels are identical, and when decoding a stereo frame in a
mono decoder, the mono output is the average of the left and right
channels.  In some cases, it is desirable to encode a stereo input
stream in mono (e.g., because the bitrate is too low to encode stereo
with sufficient quality).  The number of channels encoded can be
selected in real-time, but by default the reference encoder attempts
to make the best decision possible given the current bitrate.

#### 中文
Opus 可以在单个流中传输单声道或立体声帧。在立体声解码器中解码单声道帧时，左右通道是相同的；在单声道解码器中解码立体声帧时，单声道输出是左右通道的平均值。在某些情况下，希望以单声道编码立体声输入流（例如，因为比特率太低而无法以足够的质量编码立体声）。编码的通道数可以实时选择，但默认情况下，参考编码器尝试根据当前比特率做出最佳决策。

---

### 2.1.3. Audio Bandwidth | 2.1.3. 音频带宽

#### 原文
The audio bandwidths supported by Opus are listed in Table 1.  Just
like for the number of channels, any decoder can decode audio that is
encoded at any bandwidth.  For example, any Opus decoder operating at
8 kHz can decode an FB Opus frame, and any Opus decoder operating at
48 kHz can decode an NB frame.  Similarly, the reference encoder can
take a 48 kHz input signal and encode it as NB.  The higher the audio
bandwidth, the higher the required bitrate to achieve acceptable
quality.  The audio bandwidth can be explicitly specified in real-
time, but, by default, the reference encoder attempts to make the
best bandwidth decision possible given the current bitrate.

#### 中文
Opus 支持的音频带宽列在表 1 中。与通道数一样，任何解码器都可以解码以任何带宽编码的音频。例如，任何以 8 kHz 运行的 Opus 解码器都可以解码 FB Opus 帧，任何以 48 kHz 运行的 Opus 解码器都可以解码 NB 帧。类似地，参考编码器可以接收 48 kHz 输入信号并将其编码为 NB。音频带宽越高，实现可接受质量所需的比特率就越高。音频带宽可以实时明确指定，但默认情况下，参考编码器尝试根据当前比特率做出最佳带宽决策。

---

### 2.1.4. Frame Duration | 2.1.4. 帧时长

#### 原文
Opus can encode frames of 2.5, 5, 10, 20, 40, or 60 ms.  It can also
combine multiple frames into packets of up to 120 ms.  For real-time
applications, sending fewer packets per second reduces the bitrate,
since it reduces the overhead from IP, UDP, and RTP headers.
However, it increases latency and sensitivity to packet losses, as
losing one packet constitutes a loss of a bigger chunk of audio.
Increasing the frame duration also slightly improves coding
efficiency, but the gain becomes small for frame sizes above 20 ms.
For this reason, 20 ms frames are a good choice for most
applications.

#### 中文
Opus 可以编码 2.5、5、10、20、40 或 60 ms 的帧。它还可以将多个帧组合成最多 120 ms 的数据包。对于实时应用，每秒发送更少的数据包可以降低比特率，因为它减少了来自 IP、UDP 和 RTP 头部的开销。然而，这会增加延迟和对丢包的敏感度，因为丢失一个数据包就意味着丢失更大块的音频。增加帧时长还能略微提高编码效率，但帧大小超过 20 ms 后这种增益变得很小。因此，20 ms 帧对于大多数应用来说是一个很好的选择。

---

### 2.1.5. Complexity | 2.1.5. 复杂度

#### 原文
There are various aspects of the Opus encoding process where trade-
offs can be made between CPU complexity and quality/bitrate.  In the
reference encoder, the complexity is selected using an integer from 0
to 10, where 0 is the lowest complexity and 10 is the highest.
Examples of computations for which such trade-offs may occur are:

o  The order of the pitch analysis whitening filter [WHITENING],

o  The order of the short-term noise shaping filter,

o  The number of states in delayed decision quantization of the
   residual signal, and

o  The use of certain bitstream features such as variable time-
   frequency resolution and the pitch post-filter.

#### 中文
Opus 编码过程中有许多方面可以在 CPU 复杂度和质量/比特率之间进行权衡。在参考编码器中，复杂度使用从 0 到 10 的整数选择，其中 0 是最低复杂度，10 是最高复杂度。可能出现此类权衡的计算示例如下：

o  基音分析白化滤波器 [WHITENING] 的阶数，

o  短期噪声整形滤波器的阶数，

o  残差信号的延迟判决量化中的状态数，以及

o  某些比特流特性的使用，例如可变时频分辨率和基音后置滤波器。

---

### 2.1.6. Packet Loss Resilience | 2.1.6. 丢包容忍度

#### 原文
Audio codecs often exploit inter-frame correlations to reduce the
bitrate at a cost in error propagation: after losing one packet,
several packets need to be received before the decoder is able to
accurately reconstruct the speech signal.  The extent to which Opus
exploits inter-frame dependencies can be adjusted on the fly to
choose a trade-off between bitrate and amount of error propagation.

#### 中文
音频编解码器通常利用帧间相关性来降低比特率，但代价是错误传播：丢失一个数据包后，需要接收多个数据包，解码器才能准确重建语音信号。Opus 利用帧间依赖关系的程度可以动态调整，以在比特率和错误传播量之间选择权衡。

---

### 2.1.7. Forward Error Correction (FEC) | 2.1.7. 前向纠错（FEC）

#### 原文
Another mechanism providing robustness against packet loss is the in-
band Forward Error Correction (FEC).  Packets that are determined to
contain perceptually important speech information, such as onsets or
transients, are encoded again at a lower bitrate and this re-encoded
information is added to a subsequent packet.

#### 中文
另一种提供抗丢包能力的机制是带内前向纠错（FEC）。被判定为包含感知上重要的语音信息（如音节起音或瞬态信号）的数据包会以较低的比特率再次编码，并且这些重新编码的信息被添加到后续数据包中。

---

### 2.1.8. Constant/Variable Bitrate | 2.1.8. 恒定/可变比特率

#### 原文
Opus is more efficient when operating with variable bitrate (VBR),
which is the default.  When low-latency transmission is required over
a relatively slow connection, then constrained VBR can also be used.
This uses VBR in a way that simulates a "bit reservoir" and is
equivalent to what MP3 (MPEG 1, Layer 3) and AAC (Advanced Audio
Coding) call CBR (i.e., not true CBR due to the bit reservoir).  In
some (rare) applications, constant bitrate (CBR) is required.  There
are two main reasons to operate in CBR mode:

o  When the transport only supports a fixed size for each compressed
   frame, or

o  When encryption is used for an audio stream that is either highly
   constrained (e.g., yes/no, recorded prompts) or highly sensitive
   [SRTP-VBR].

#### 中文
Opus 在使用可变比特率（VBR）时更高效，这也是默认模式。当需要通过相对较慢的连接进行低延迟传输时，也可以使用约束 VBR（constrained VBR）。这种方式以模拟"比特池（bit reservoir）"的方式来使用 VBR，等同于 MP3（MPEG 1，第 3 层）和 AAC（高级音频编码）所谓的 CBR（即，由于比特池机制，不是真正的 CBR）。在某些（罕见的）应用中，需要恒定比特率（CBR）。以 CBR 模式运行有两个主要原因：

o  当传输层仅支持每个压缩帧的固定大小时，或者

o  当加密用于高度受限（例如，是/否、录制提示音）或高度敏感 [SRTP-VBR] 的音频流时。

---

#### 原文
Bitrate may still be allowed to vary, even with sensitive data, as
long as the variation is not driven by the input signal (for example,
to match changing network conditions).  To achieve this, an
application should still run Opus in CBR mode, but change the target
rate before each packet.

#### 中文
即使对于敏感数据，只要变化不是由输入信号驱动的（例如，为了匹配变化的网络条件），比特率仍然可能被允许变化。为实现此目标，应用程序仍然应该在 CBR 模式下运行 Opus，但在每个数据包之前更改目标速率。

---

### 2.1.9. Discontinuous Transmission (DTX) | 2.1.9. 非连续传输（DTX）

#### 原文
Discontinuous Transmission (DTX) reduces the bitrate during silence
or background noise.  When DTX is enabled, only one frame is encoded
every 400 milliseconds.

#### 中文
非连续传输（DTX）在静音或背景噪声期间降低比特率。当启用 DTX 时，每 400 毫秒仅编码一个帧。

685	3.  Internal Framing
686	
687	   The Opus encoder produces "packets", which are each a contiguous set
688	   of bytes meant to be transmitted as a single unit.  The packets
689	   described here do not include such things as IP, UDP, or RTP headers,
690	   which are normally found in a transport-layer packet.  A single
691	   packet may contain multiple audio frames, so long as they share a
692	   common set of parameters, including the operating mode, audio
693	   bandwidth, frame size, and channel count (mono vs. stereo).  This
694	   section describes the possible combinations of these parameters and
695	   the internal framing used to pack multiple frames into a single
696	   packet.  This framing is not self-delimiting.  Instead, it assumes
697	   that a lower layer (such as UDP or RTP [RFC3550] or Ogg [RFC3533] or
698	   Matroska [MATROSKA-WEBSITE]) will communicate the length, in bytes,
699	   of the packet, and it uses this information to reduce the framing
700	   overhead in the packet itself.  A decoder implementation MUST support
701	   the framing described in this section.  An alternative, self-
702	   delimiting variant of the framing is described in Appendix B.
703	   Support for that variant is OPTIONAL.
704	
705	   All bit diagrams in this document number the bits so that bit 0 is
706	   the most significant bit of the first byte, and bit 7 is the least
707	   significant.  Bit 8 is thus the most significant bit of the second
708	   byte, etc.  Well-formed Opus packets obey certain requirements,
709	   marked [R1] through [R7] below.  These are summarized in Section 3.4
710	   along with appropriate means of handling malformed packets.
711	
712	3.1.  The TOC Byte

715	   byte forms a table-of-contents (TOC) header that signals which of the
716	   various modes and configurations a given packet uses.  It is composed
717	   of a configuration number, "config", a stereo flag, "s", and a frame
718	   count code, "c", arranged as illustrated in Figure 1.  A description
719	   of each of these fields follows.

231	1.  Introduction
232	
233	   The Opus codec is a real-time interactive audio codec designed to
234	   meet the requirements described in [REQUIREMENTS].  It is composed of
235	   a layer based on Linear Prediction (LP) [LPC] and a layer based on
236	   the Modified Discrete Cosine Transform (MDCT) [MDCT].  The main idea
237	   behind using two layers is as follows: in speech, linear prediction
238	   techniques (such as Code-Excited Linear Prediction, or CELP) code low
239	   frequencies more efficiently than transform (e.g., MDCT) domain
240	   techniques, while the situation is reversed for music and higher
241	   speech frequencies.  Thus, a codec with both layers available can
242	   operate over a wider range than either one alone and can achieve
243	   better quality by combining them than by using either one
244	   individually.
245	
246	   The primary normative part of this specification is provided by the
247	   source code in Appendix A.  Only the decoder portion of this software
248	   is normative, though a significant amount of code is shared by both
249	   the encoder and decoder.  Section 6 provides a decoder conformance
250	   test.  The decoder contains a great deal of integer and fixed-point
251	   arithmetic that needs to be performed exactly, including all rounding
252	   considerations, so any useful specification requires domain-specific
253	   symbolic language to adequately define these operations.
254	   Additionally, any conflict between the symbolic representation and
255	   the included reference implementation must be resolved.  For the
256	   practical reasons of compatibility and testability, it would be

# RFC 6716 Section 3 中英对照翻译
# RFC 6716 Section 3 Chinese-English Parallel Translation

---

## 3. Internal Framing | 3. 内部帧结构

#### 原文

The Opus encoder produces "packets", which are each a contiguous set of bytes meant to be transmitted as a single unit. The packets described here do not include such things as IP, UDP, or RTP headers, which are normally found in a transport-layer packet. A single packet may contain multiple audio frames, so long as they share a common set of parameters, including the operating mode, audio bandwidth, frame size, and channel count (mono vs. stereo). This section describes the possible combinations of these parameters and the internal framing used to pack multiple frames into a single packet. This framing is not self-delimiting. Instead, it assumes that a lower layer (such as UDP or RTP [RFC3550] or Ogg [RFC3533] or Matroska [MATROSKA-WEBSITE]) will communicate the length, in bytes, of the packet, and it uses this information to reduce the framing overhead in the packet itself. A decoder implementation MUST support the framing described in this section. An alternative, self-delimiting variant of the framing is described in Appendix B. Support for that variant is OPTIONAL.

#### 中文

Opus 编码器生成"数据包"，每个数据包是一组连续的字节，作为单个单元进行传输。这里描述的数据包不包括 IP、UDP 或 RTP 头部信息，这些头部通常出现在传输层数据包中。单个数据包可以包含多个音频帧，只要它们共享一组共同的参数，包括操作模式、音频带宽、帧大小和通道数（单声道 vs. 立体声）。本节描述了这些参数的可能组合，以及用于将多个帧打包到单个数据包中的内部帧结构。这种帧结构不是自定界的。相反，它假设下层（如 UDP 或 RTP [RFC3550]、Ogg [RFC3533] 或 Matroska [MATROSKA-WEBSITE]）会告知数据包的字节长度，并利用这一信息来减少数据包本身的帧结构开销。解码器实现必须支持本节中描述的帧结构。附录 B 中描述了另一种自定界变体的帧结构。对该变体的支持是可选的。

#### 原文

All bit diagrams in this document number the bits so that bit 0 is the most significant bit of the first byte, and bit 7 is the least significant. Bit 8 is thus the most significant bit of the second byte, etc. Well-formed Opus packets obey certain requirements, marked [R1] through [R7] below. These are summarized in Section 3.4 along with appropriate means of handling malformed packets.

#### 中文

本文档中的所有位图都以如下方式编号位：位 0 是第一个字节的最高有效位，位 7 是最低有效位。因此，位 8 是第二个字节的最高有效位，依此类推。格式正确的 Opus 数据包遵循某些要求，下面标记为 [R1] 到 [R7]。这些要求在 3.4 节中进行了总结，同时给出了处理畸形数据包的适当方法。

---

### 3.1. The TOC Byte | 3.1. TOC 字节

#### 原文

A well-formed Opus packet MUST contain at least one byte [R1]. This byte forms a table-of-contents (TOC) header that signals which of the various modes and configurations a given packet uses. It is composed of a configuration number, "config", a stereo flag, "s", and a frame count code, "c", arranged as illustrated in Figure 1. A description of each of these fields follows.

#### 中文

格式正确的 Opus 数据包必须包含至少一个字节 [R1]。该字节构成一个目录（TOC）头部，用于标识给定数据包使用了哪种模式和配置。它由一个配置编号 "config"、一个立体声标志 "s" 和一个帧数代码 "c" 组成，排列方式如图 1 所示。以下是对每个字段的描述。

```
                          0
                          0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7
                         +-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+
                         | config  |s| c |
                         +-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+

                      Figure 1: The TOC Byte

                      图 1: TOC 字节
```

#### 原文

The top five bits of the TOC byte, labeled "config", encode one of 32 possible configurations of operating mode, audio bandwidth, and frame size. As described, the LP (SILK) layer and MDCT (CELT) layer can be combined in three possible operating modes:

1. A SILK-only mode for use in low bitrate connections with an audio bandwidth of WB or less,

2. A Hybrid (SILK+CELT) mode for SWB or FB speech at medium bitrates, and

3. A CELT-only mode for very low delay speech transmission as well as music transmission (NB to FB).

#### 中文

TOC 字节的高五位标记为 "config"，编码了操作模式、音频带宽和帧大小的 32 种可能配置之一。如前所述，LP (SILK) 层和 MDCT (CELT) 层可以以三种可能的操作模式组合：

1. SILK-only 模式，用于音频带宽为 WB 或更低的低比特率连接，

2. Hybrid (SILK+CELT) 模式，用于中等比特率的 SWB 或 FB 语音，以及

3. CELT-only 模式，用于极低延迟的语音传输以及音乐传输（NB 到 FB）。

#### 原文

The 32 possible configurations each identify which one of these operating modes the packet uses, as well as the audio bandwidth and the frame size. Table 2 lists the parameters for each configuration.

#### 中文

32 种可能的配置各自标识了数据包使用上述哪种操作模式，以及音频带宽和帧大小。表 2 列出了每种配置的参数。

```
   +-----------------------+-----------+-----------+-------------------+
   | Configuration         | Mode      | Bandwidth | Frame Sizes       |
   | Number(s)             |           |           |                   |
   +-----------------------+-----------+-----------+-------------------+
   | 0...3                 | SILK-only | NB        | 10, 20, 40, 60 ms |
   |                       |           |           |                   |
   | 4...7                 | SILK-only | MB        | 10, 20, 40, 60 ms |
   |                       |           |           |                   |
   | 8...11                | SILK-only | WB        | 10, 20, 40, 60 ms |
   |                       |           |           |                   |
   | 12...13               | Hybrid    | SWB       | 10, 20 ms         |
   |                       |           |           |                   |
   | 14...15               | Hybrid    | FB        | 10, 20 ms         |
   |                       |           |           |                   |
   | 16...19               | CELT-only | NB        | 2.5, 5, 10, 20 ms |
   |                       |           |           |                   |
   | 20...23               | CELT-only | WB        | 2.5, 5, 10, 20 ms |
   |                       |           |           |                   |
   | 24...27               | CELT-only | SWB       | 2.5, 5, 10, 20 ms |
   |                       |           |           |                   |
   | 28...31               | CELT-only | FB        | 2.5, 5, 10, 20 ms |
   +-----------------------+-----------+-----------+-------------------+

            Table 2: TOC Byte Configuration Parameters

            表 2: TOC 字节配置参数
```

#### 原文

The configuration numbers in each range (e.g., 0...3 for NB SILK-only) correspond to the various choices of frame size, in the same order. For example, configuration 0 has a 10 ms frame size and configuration 3 has a 60 ms frame size.

#### 中文

每个范围内的配置编号（例如，NB SILK-only 的 0...3）按相同顺序对应不同的帧大小选择。例如，配置 0 的帧大小为 10 ms，配置 3 的帧大小为 60 ms。

#### 原文

One additional bit, labeled "s", signals mono vs. stereo, with 0 indicating mono and 1 indicating stereo.

#### 中文

还有一个标记为 "s" 的附加位，用于标识单声道还是立体声，0 表示单声道，1 表示立体声。

#### 原文

The remaining two bits of the TOC byte, labeled "c", code the number of frames per packet (codes 0 to 3) as follows:

o 0: 1 frame in the packet

o 1: 2 frames in the packet, each with equal compressed size

o 2: 2 frames in the packet, with different compressed sizes

o 3: an arbitrary number of frames in the packet

#### 中文

TOC 字节的剩余两位标记为 "c"，用于编码每个数据包的帧数（编码 0 到 3），具体如下：

o 0: 数据包中有 1 个帧

o 1: 数据包中有 2 个帧，每个帧的压缩大小相等

o 2: 数据包中有 2 个帧，压缩大小不同

o 3: 数据包中有任意数量的帧

#### 原文

This document refers to a packet as a code 0 packet, code 1 packet, etc., based on the value of "c".

#### 中文

本文档根据 "c" 的值将数据包称为 code 0 包、code 1 包等。

---

### 3.2. Frame Packing | 3.2. 帧打包

#### 原文

This section describes how frames are packed according to each possible value of "c" in the TOC byte.

#### 中文

本节描述了如何根据 TOC 字节中 "c" 的每种可能取值来打包帧。

---

### 3.2.1. Frame Length Coding | 3.2.1. 帧长度编码

#### 原文

When a packet contains multiple VBR frames (i.e., code 2 or 3), the compressed length of one or more of these frames is indicated with a one- or two-byte sequence, with the meaning of the first byte as follows:

o 0: No frame (Discontinuous Transmission (DTX) or lost packet)

o 1...251: Length of the frame in bytes

o 252...255: A second byte is needed. The total length is (second_byte*4)+first_byte

#### 中文

当数据包包含多个 VBR 帧（即 code 2 或 3）时，这些帧中一个或多个帧的压缩长度由一个或两个字节的序列表示，第一个字节的含义如下：

o 0: 无帧（不连续传输 (DTX) 或丢失的数据包）

o 1...251: 帧的字节长度

o 252...255: 需要第二个字节。总长度为 (second_byte*4)+first_byte

#### 原文

The special length 0 indicates that no frame is available, either because it was dropped during transmission by some intermediary or because the encoder chose not to transmit it. Any Opus frame in any mode MAY have a length of 0.

#### 中文

特殊长度 0 表示没有可用的帧，可能是因为某个中间设备在传输过程中将其丢弃，或者是因为编码器选择不传输该帧。任何模式下的任何 Opus 帧的长度都可以为 0。

#### 原文

The maximum representable length is 255*4+255=1275 bytes. For 20 ms frames, this represents a bitrate of 510 kbit/s, which is approximately the highest useful rate for lossily compressed fullband stereo music. Beyond this point, lossless codecs are more appropriate. It is also roughly the maximum useful rate of the MDCT layer as, shortly thereafter, quality no longer improves with additional bits due to limitations on the codebook sizes.

#### 中文

最大可表示长度为 255*4+255=1275 字节。对于 20 ms 的帧，这表示 510 kbit/s 的比特率，大约是经过有损压缩的全频带立体声音乐的最高有效码率。超过这个值，无损编解码器更为合适。这也大约是 MDCT 层的最高有效码率，因为在此之后，由于码本大小的限制，质量不会再随着额外比特的增加而提高。

#### 原文

No length is transmitted for the last frame in a VBR packet, or for any of the frames in a CBR packet, as it can be inferred from the total size of the packet and the size of all other data in the packet. However, the length of any individual frame MUST NOT exceed 1275 bytes [R2] to allow for repacketization by gateways, conference bridges, or other software.

#### 中文

VBR 数据包中的最后一帧，或者 CBR 数据包中的任何帧，都不传输长度信息，因为可以从数据包的总大小和数据包中所有其他数据的大小推断出来。然而，任何单个帧的长度不得超过 1275 字节 [R2]，以便网关、会议桥或其他软件进行重新打包。

---

### 3.2.2. Code 0: One Frame in the Packet | 3.2.2. Code 0: 数据包中有一个帧

#### 原文

For code 0 packets, the TOC byte is immediately followed by N-1 bytes of compressed data for a single frame (where N is the size of the packet), as illustrated in Figure 2.

#### 中文

对于 code 0 数据包，TOC 字节之后紧跟着单个帧的 N-1 字节压缩数据（其中 N 是数据包的大小），如图 2 所示。

```
